Alternatively, create a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone with resources." https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-pricing.html ; the regional NAT doc says "standard NAT gateways (referred to as zonal NAT gateways)" https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateways-regional.html
flagged.problem: The fact is true, but the terminology is wrong. The explanation calls it a "subnet-based NAT gateway", which is not an AWS term. The statement just says "a NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone". Since late 2025, AWS calls this type a "zonal NAT gateway", to tell it apart from regional NAT gateways, which span AZs. A regional NAT gateway also keeps zonal affinity, except for up to 60 minutes while it expands into a new AZ, when traffic is processed across zones.
flagged.suggestedFix: Statement: "Routing an EC2 instance through a zonal NAT gateway in the instance's own Availability Zone avoids cross-AZ data-transfer charges on that hop." (answer true). Explanation: "AWS recommends keeping resources in the same AZ as their zonal NAT gateway, or deploying one zonal NAT gateway per AZ, to avoid cross-AZ data-transfer charges. NAT gateway hourly and per-GB processing charges still apply."

NLB: "Yes, you will be charged for regional data transfer between Availability Zones with Network Load Balancer when cross-zone load balancing is enabled." https://aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/faqs/
flagged.problem: The answer (false) is correct. The second sentence of the explanation is wrong: "Application Load Balancer cross-zone traffic has a different billing exemption" suggests ALB has some other exemption. In fact ALB is simply exempt, because cross-zone load balancing is always on. The first sentence also leaves out that NLB charges apply when cross-zone load balancing is enabled, which is off by default.
flagged.suggestedFix: Explanation: "Application Load Balancers always balance across zones and are not charged for that regional data transfer. A Network Load Balancer has cross-zone load balancing off by default; when you enable it, inter-AZ data transfer is charged."
